intro.title: Feature Flag Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useFeatureFlag` that allows you to toggle features on and off in your application. You'll learn how to create reusable logic with hooks, manage state to control feature visibility, and conditionally render components based on that state. The main technologies involved are React hooks like `useState` and `useEffect`, along with JavaScript conditionals and JSX. By the end, you'll have a practical hook that can be integrated into any React project to enable or disable features dynamically.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are essential in modern web applications for controlled rollouts and A/B testing. Developers use them to toggle new dashboard features, experimental UI panels, or beta functionality for specific user segments without redeploying code. For example, an e-commerce site might show a redesigned checkout form only to 10% of users to test performance before full release. This pattern enables gradual feature deployment, reduces risk, and allows quick rollbacks if issues arise.
